Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.

items.title: Embodied Movable Antennas
items.summary: This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

items.title: Implicit Additively Weighted Geodesic Voronoi Diagrams and Applications
items.summary: Let $P$ be a simple polygon with $m$ vertices. After $O(m)$-time preprocessing of $P$, for any set $S$ of $n$ additively weighted point sites, we compute an implicit additively weighted geodesic Voronoi diagram in $O(n\log n+n\log^2 m)$ time, supporting nearest-neighbor queries in $O(\log(n+m))$ time. In contrast, explicitly constructing the diagram requires $Ω(m)$ time. Our algorithm introduces a new sweep-line paradigm that avoids explicitly constructing the diagram, together with a novel technique for point location in implicit subdivisions. As applications, we obtain new dynamic data structures for additively weighted geodesic nearest-neighbor searching and the first efficient algorithms for shortest paths in geodesic disk graphs. After the same $O(m)$-time preprocessing, single-source shortest paths in a geodesic disk graph of $n$ sites can be computed in $O(n\log n+n\log^2 m)$ time in the unweighted case and $O(n^{3/2}(\log n+\log^2 m))$ time in the weighted case. We also extend our techniques to implicit farthest geodesic Voronoi diagrams for unweighted sites, obtaining analogous bounds and dynamic farthest-neighbor data structures.

items.title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap
items.summary: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.

items.title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for linear algebra that access a matrix $A$ through quantum random access memory (QRAM) prepare quantum states proportional to the solutions of linear systems and related problems. Dequantized classical algorithms, when given sampling and query access to $A$, return sampling and query access to an approximate solution. Both kinds of algorithms use a number of queries that is polynomial in the normalized Frobenius norm $ρ=\|A\|_F/\|A\|$ and does not directly depend on the dimension. For linear systems at fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ)$ queries, whereas the best dequantized algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ^4)$. We prove that this quartic gap is tight in the worst case, up to a logarithmic factor. For every constant $κ_0>1$, we construct dense linear systems with condition number at most $κ_0$ for which sampling from the solution within a sufficiently small constant total variation distance requires $Ω(ρ^4/\logρ)$ classical queries but only $Θ(ρ)$ quantum queries. The same separation holds, for errors below smaller thresholds, for positive-definite systems, least squares, ridge regression, matrix powers and square roots, imaginary-time and real-time Hamiltonian evolution, and sampling from the top principal component. Our results therefore show that many quantum algorithms for linear algebra, achieve a near-quartic speedup in the worst case, over classical algorithms with sampling and query access. All of these classical lower bounds follow from the same framework, which is based on a lower bound for sampling from distributions that depend on a fixed set of Fourier coefficients of an unknown Boolean function.

items.title: Two choices suffice: $k$-out sampling leaves $O(n/k)$ intercomponent edges for $k\geq 2$
items.summary: Given a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, random $k$-out sampling forms a spanning subgraph by having each vertex independently choose $k$ incident edges uniformly with replacement. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq2$, the expected number of original edges joining distinct sampled components is $O(n/k)$. This resolves the conjecture of Holm, King, Thorup, Zamir, and Zwick in its full range, improving their logarithmic sampling requirement to the optimal threshold of two choices per vertex. The bound fails for $k=1$, and the dependence $O(n/k)$ is tight up to constant factors. Our result holds with replacement and consequently also without replacement. In particular, this implies that contracting just two independent local choices per vertex suffices to reduce an arbitrary simple graph to a quotient with $O(n)$ edges in expectation, which is crucial in reducing the instance size for many contraction-based algorithms. Our proof uses switching arguments to relate intercomponent edges to bridges and a degree-weighted component potential, whose expectation we also bound with a switching argument.

items.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
items.summary: Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $Δ\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $Δ$-regular graph for all $β<β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ where $β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $Δ$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $β<β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $Δ$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.

items.title: Optimal Online Weighted Connectivity Augmentation
items.summary: In the online Weighted Connectivity Augmentation Problem (WCAP), we are given a $k$-edge-connected graph on $n$ vertices and a set of additional edges, called links, with nonnegative costs. Pairs of vertices arrive one by one, and an online algorithm must immediately and irrevocably buy links so that each pair becomes $(k+1)$-edge-connected. The goal is to minimize the total cost of the purchased links. We obtain a deterministic polynomial-time $O(\log n)$-competitive algorithm for WCAP, improving the previous $O(\log^2 n)$ bound (SODA 2026). Our bound is asymptotically optimal, even for randomized algorithms in the random-order model. The general problem reduces to the case where the underlying graph is a cycle, for which link costs in $\{0,1\}$ already yield an $Ω(\log n)$ lower bound. Surprisingly, for unit costs on a cycle, we obtain a deterministic polynomial-time $4$-competitive algorithm, improving the previous $O(\log n)$ bound (SODA 2026), and prove that this ratio is optimal among deterministic algorithms. Thus, with unit costs, cycles are easier than trees, where the optimal competitive ratio is $Θ(\log n)$.

items.title: Treedepth is NP-Hard on Planar Graphs of Maximum Degree 3
items.summary: Treedepth is an important parameter in algorithmic graph theory. It is known that the problem of computing the treedepth of a graph is NP-hard. It has been an open problem whether treedepth can be computed in polynomial time when the input graph is restricted to be planar, or of bounded degree. Assuming $P \neq NP$, we answer both questions in the negative: Under polynomial-time Turing reductions, it is NP-hard to compute the treedepth of planar graphs with maximum degree 3. This degree bound is best possible, since treedepth can be computed efficiently on graphs of maximum degree 2.

items.title: Stochastic processes on reductive homogeneous and symmetric spaces
items.summary: In this paper we present a method to effectively and efficiently provide pathwise approximations of the Riemannian Brownian motion on a reductive homogeneous space $M\cong G/H$ endowed with a $G$-invariant metric. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. The efficiency lies in the fact that explicit representations of the Wong--Zakai approximations can be obtained in this setting using the Lie exponential map.

items.title: Capacity Meets the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and the Cross-Ratio
items.summary: $K$ users each observe a fixed linear function of common data over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and a server must recover another fixed linear function with zero error from one message sent by each user. The capacity, the minimum total number of symbols the users send per computed instance, depends only on the configuration of subspaces formed by these linear functions. We study the instance in which three users observe $\boldsymbol{a}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{a}+\boldsymbol{b}$ and the server wants $\boldsymbol{a}+λ\boldsymbol{b}$. The four functions span four lines in a plane with cross-ratio $λ$, the smallest instance of the four subspace problem of representation theory. It is the smallest configuration whose capacity is not determined by the dimensions of the subspaces formed by sums and intersections: these dimensions are the same for every $λ$, but the capacity depends on the cross-ratio and on the prime subfield. For the harmonic cross-ratios, $λ=-1$, $λ=2$ or $2λ=1$, it is $2$: every zero-error code reveals $(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b})$ to the server, so no code beats having two users send their observations. For $λ$ outside the prime subfield it is the cut-set bound $3/2$, achieved by codes linear over the prime subfield, while codes linear over the field need $2$. For the other $λ$ in the prime subfield it lies in $[3p/(2p-1),2]$, so no code at any block length approaches the cut-set bound. The qualitative separation persists under vanishing error for uniform data: the cut-set bound is tight exactly for $λ$ outside the prime subfield. The four-line instance is also exact repair of one node of a $[4,2]$ MDS storage code, and the results translate to that setting.

items.title: 3SUM Made Simpler (Without Matrix Multiplication), $k$-SUM Hypothesis Refuted for Odd $k$, and Real 3SUM/APSP Derandomized
items.summary: Recently, a truly subquadratic algorithm for the 3SUM problem and a truly subcubic algorithm for the all-pairs shortest paths (APSP) problem were found by Anthropic, as reported by Alman and Vassilevska Williams (2026). These algorithms relied on a new subroutine for rectangular matrix multiplication with selected output entries, which was obtained by modifying known matrix multiplication techniques of Schönhage (1981) and Coppersmith (1982). 1. We present a different truly subquadratic randomized algorithm for 3SUM for integer inputs. It completely avoids the use of matrix multiplication but instead modifies known dynamic programming algorithms for subset convolution and the zeta transform, which rely only on simple subtraction tricks via inclusion--exclusion (and does not even require fast Fourier transform), and so is conceptually easier to understand (the whole solution is about 5 pages long). 2. Following a similar approach, we obtain a randomized algorithm for $k$-SUM for integer inputs for odd constant $k$ in $O(n^{\lceil k/2\rceil-\varepsilon_k})$ time for some constant $\varepsilon_k>0$, disproving the $k$-SUM Hypothesis for all odd $k$. 3. Existing reductions from 3SUM and APSP to selected-entries rectangular matrix multiplication were randomized in the case of real-valued input. We present new deterministic reductions, yielding a truly subquadratic deterministic algorithm for Real 3SUM and a truly subcubic deterministic algorithm for Real APSP.

items.title: The C-3PO Framework: Algorithms for $\#\mathrm{BIS}$-Hard Problems on Graphs with Low Threshold Rank or High Girth
items.summary: We give approximate counting and sampling algorithms for spin models on graphs of low threshold rank or high girth. Given any $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $k_η= k_η(G)$ count normalized-Laplacian eigenvalues strictly below $η$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, an $\varepsilon$-approximate counting algorithm outputs an estimate $\widehat Z$ of the partition function $Z$ satisfying $(1-\varepsilon)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z$ with probability at least $3/4$. An $\varepsilon$-approximate sampling algorithm outputs a configuration whose distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the target distribution. We give the following results: (a) Ferromagnetic Potts. Fix $q\ge2$ and $η\in(0,1]$. There exists $β_0(q,η)$ such that, for every inverse temperature $β\geβ_0$, the zero-field $q$-state Potts model admits approximate counting and sampling algorithms: (i) On arbitrary graphs in time $\exp(O(k_η))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) Fix $Δ\ge 3$. On $Δ$-regular graphs of girth $g$ in time $\exp(O(n e^{-g})) \operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (b) Bipartite hard-core. Fix $Δ\ge3$ and $η\in(0,1]$. There exists $λ_0(Δ,η)$ such that, for every fugacity $λ\geλ_0$, the hard-core model admits approximate counting and sampling: (i) On $Δ$-regular vertex-transitive bipartite graphs in time $\exp(O (k_η))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) On $Δ$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $g$ in $\exp(O(n e^{- g}))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ All four results follow from verifying the hypotheses of a new framework we call C-3PO. At a high level, the C-3PO algorithm proceeds by enumerating small cuts and reconstructing the original measure through cluster expansions. Underlying the algorithm is an improvement of subspace enumeration methods via active regression.

items.title: A Robust High-order Approximation of the Gray Thermal Radiative Transfer Equations
items.summary: We present a high-order, positivity preserving, and asymptotic preserving approximation of the gray radiative transfer equations. The time and space approximation is done using a diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta method with stabilized, continuous finite elements, and the angular approximation uses the method of discrete ordinates. We detail a simple and robust inner/outer iteration strategy to solve these equations and prove that the proposed scheme is exactly conservative, independent of iterative tolerances. A maximum and minimum principle is enforced using a conservative redistribution limiting technique, and the method is demonstrated to be robust in the thick diffusion limit.

items.title: On Universal Minkowski Classes of Polytopes: Theory and Applications
items.summary: This paper establishes the existence, in every dimension, of universal Minkowski classes of configuration-constrained polytopes, with direct applications to set-theoretic control. For any prescribed accuracy, such a class contains an approximation of every compact convex set to that accuracy and admits a jointly affine parameterization of facets and vertices. The construction is explicit and relies on a combinatorial averaging procedure that produces minimal configuration enclosures. In control, these polytopic templates enable convex reformulations of otherwise non-convex problems, including invariant-set computation and control Lyapunov function design. Tutorial examples illustrate both the geometric construction and its control applications.

items.title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
items.summary: We show that any $n$-point Euclidean metric admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}}\right)$, matching a known lower bound. We also present two applications of this result. First, we give a cut-player strategy with an optimal spectral guarantee for the undirected cut-matching game. Second, we give an improved spectral approximation for vertex expansion in high-degree graphs.

items.title: Safety Verification for Voltage Control in Inverter Dominated Radial Distribution Networks under Actuator and Sensor Adversarial Attacks
items.summary: This paper develops a safety verification framework for inverter-based radial distribution networks under sensor and actuator attacks. Each customer is equipped with a droop-based controller to regulate its voltage within a desirable bound of a reference, i.e., to achieve safety. In our setting, attacks and disturbances enter the droop-based controllers, while actuator attacks corrupt the reactive power injected into the network. Consequently, invariance of the controller state alone does not guarantee compliance with inverter capacities or customer voltage limits. To address this challenge, we derive conditions to guarantee that the reactive power state remains inside a predefined ellipsoid, while at the same time ensuring that the attacked reactive power injections and customer voltages respect predetermined operating limits that hold uniformly for the entire predefined ellipsoid. Together, these conditions guarantee safety under all admissible disturbances and state-dependent sensor and actuator attacks. Finally, we express the resulting containment condition as a linear matrix inequality (LMI) feasibility problem. A five-customer radial network based on the CIGRE benchmark corroborates our theoretical developments in simulations.

items.title: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for $k$-Hadamard operators
items.summary: In this paper we present results related to Donoho--Stark type uncertainty principles that were proved in the article "The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme" by Wigderson and Wigderson for $k$-Hadamard operators in the finite-dimensional setting. Namely, the authors showed that Donoho-Stark principles can be generalized to versions for approximate supports with respect to norms $\ell^{p}$ for $p=1$ and $p=2$. In the second case they assumed the so-called speciality condition, namely that a suitable matrix satisfies $A^{*}A = kI$. First we show that such theorems cannot be generalized to $p>1$ if matrices are not special $k$-Hadamard. Next we prove Donoho-Stark type principle for special $k$-Hadamard operators for $\ell^{p}$ norms within the range $1\leq p\leq 2$. Finally, we show that such theorems are false for $p>2$ even in the presence of the speciality condition.

items.title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
items.summary: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.

items.title: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing
items.summary: Modern language models motivate renewed interest in universal prediction problems in which a predictor can exploit previously observed data before predicting a fresh sequence. We study an idealized version of this setting by introducing \emph{batch regret}: a conditional analogue of classical average regret in which a predictor observes a batch of $n$ training sequences and is then evaluated on an independent test sequence generated by the same unknown source. Additive smoothing estimators, which add a bias to the observed token frequencies before predicting the next token, played a fundamental role as a simple prediction strategy with almost-optimal average regret for memoryless and Markov sources. Their equivalent under batch regret are the conditional additive smoothing estimators, which estimate the conditional distribution of the test sequence given the training batch. In this work, we study their asymptotical batch regret for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources. For binary memoryless sources, we show how the optimal bias of the estimator, and consequently the corresponding batch regret, change as a function of the training batch size $n$, by extending the Poisson-based analysis of Krichevsky. For binary Markov sources with positive transitions, we characterize the leading coefficient of batch regret and its dependence on whether the initial law is known, free, or stationary. Finally, we introduce a Rényi analogue of batch regret and identify the corresponding optimal predictors as conditional $α$-NML estimators, thereby giving an operational interpretation to a conditional version of Sibson's $α$-mutual information.

items.title: Channel dichotomies
items.summary: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

items.title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
items.summary: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$. For $h$-semicomplete digraphs, a result of Kitsunai et al. [ESA 2015] also yields a $k$-triple, but only existentially, and finding one in fixed-parameter time remained open. We improve the bound on $f(k)$ to a single exponential and extend the result to $h$-semicomplete digraphs: we show that every $h$-semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth greater than $(h+1) \cdot k \cdot 2^{27k+9}$ contains a $k$-triple, which we find in polynomial time, and no bound subexponential in $k$ or sublinear in $h$ is possible. We also extend the approximation algorithm for directed pathwidth of Fomin and Pilipczuk to $h$-semicomplete digraphs, so its certificates of large directed pathwidth remain valid. Our proof is much shorter than the analysis of Kitsunai et al., and while their algorithm is exact, ours runs in polynomial time. As an application, we show that Arc-Disjoint Paths on $h$-semicomplete digraphs is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of paths and $h$, generalizing the semicomplete case. Finally, unlike in semicomplete digraphs, directed pathwidth does not bound directed cliquewidth: for every $k$, some acyclic $1$-semicomplete digraph, so of directed pathwidth zero, has directed cliquewidth at least $k$.

items.title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
items.summary: Recent developments in both high-thrust (HT) and low-thrust (LT) propulsion technologies broaden design options for on-orbit servicing (OOS) missions. However, incorporating LT transfers into OOS mission planning requires accounting for the trade-off between prescribed transfer duration and propellant consumption. Multi-servicing, multi-transfer OOS mission planning is inherently sequential and requires adaptive planning tools that account for propulsion-dependent transfer durations and mass-dependent propellant consumption. Thus, transfer dynamics must be integrated into mission planning and scheduling to increase flexibility and adaptability. In addition, the planning is often done with imperfect information about the system's state and stochastic service demands. This paper focuses on modeling orbital transfers, particularly LT transfers, within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework for OOS mission planning. To enable offline policy computation, the transfer model must provide explicit state transitions and rewards for all admissible actions. The state space is therefore augmented with the servicing vehicle's remaining propellant to enable consistent mass updates. HT transfers are modeled using a precomputed transfer matrix that maps each transfer to the time of flight and propellant consumed. LT transfers are represented using an analytical GEO phasing model with prescribed transfer-duration alternatives. For each alternative, the model calculates propellant consumption and maneuver feasibility as functions of the required phase change and the current servicing-vehicle mass. The proposed modeling approach is evaluated on simplified OOS planning scenarios using circular phasing with HT and LT propulsion. The resulting POMDPs are solved using the Successive Approximations of the Reachable Space under Optimal Policies (SARSOP) algorithm, and the policies obtained under HT and LT are compared. This comparison provides a quantitative assess

items.title: Compressing the Lawler-Moore Dynamic Program for Weighted Tardy Jobs
items.summary: The classic scheduling problem of minimizing the total weight of tardy jobs ($P_m||\sum_jw_jU_j$) asks for a schedule of jobs each with a processing time, weight, and due date on a constant number of parallel identical machines. A job is late in a schedule if it completes after its due date, and an optimal schedule is one where the total weight of all late jobs is minimized. The classic dynamic programming algorithm of Lawler and Moore [Manag. Sci., 1969] solves this problem in $O(nd_{\max}^m)$ where $n$ is the number of jobs, $d_{\max}$ is the maximum due date of any job, and $m$ is the number of identical machines. We show that it is sufficient to only compute part of the dynamic program and obtain the running time $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^{m + 1})$ where $\tilde{O}$ suppresses polylogarithmic factors. This affirmatively answers the open question posed by Hermelin, Molter, and Shabtay [INFORMS J. Comput., 2024], whether a running time of $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^2)$ is possible on a single machine.

items.title: Degree Realization with Maximum Matching
items.summary: The Maximum Matching Degree Realization problem requires, for a sequence $d$ of $n$ positive integers, to compute a realizing graph(whose degree sequence corresponds to $d$) with the maximum possible matching. We present a polynomial-time algorithm for this problem. The decision version of this problem requires to determine whether a sequence $d$ admits a realization with a matching of size $ν$ (without computing such a realization). Recently, it was shown that it can be done by verifying a series of inequalities. We improve the existing characterization by reducing the number of inequalities.

items.title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
items.summary: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}ε$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}ε$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-ε}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<\frac{1}ε$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

items.title: Catalytic space-efficient algorithms for Distance and Determinant
items.summary: Catalytic computation reuses potentially large but in-use space (or catalytic space) which must be restored to its initial contents while the clean space is small. This allows all problems in $\mathsf{NL}$ and even larger classes to be in catalytic logspace [Buhrman et al, STOC2014]. In [Chmel et al, CCC2026] the catalytic space for reachability was restricted to sublinear space (specifically, $n \big/ 2^{θ(\sqrt{\log n})}$ space) while remaining in polynomial time. This matches the non-catalytic bounds from [Barnes et al, SICOMP1998]. We extend the reachability bound to shortest distance, proving a simultaneous sublinear catalytic space and polynomial time bound (henceforth called, sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$). This is the first simultaneous sublinear space and polynomial time bound for distance even without the catalytic discipline. Moreover, our bound works even for polynomially weighted graphs. Along the way we prove simultaneous near linear catalytic space ($\mathcal{O}(n\log^{O(1)}{n})$) and polynomial time bounds for the determinant. We also show some applications to planar matching problems. Our starting point was catalytic computation of reachability in directed graphs by [Cook-Pyne, ITCS2026]. [Edenhofer, arXiv:2602.21088] used it to give a tradeoff between catalytic and non-catalytic space, while [Chmel et al, CCC2026] compress the graph to a smaller graph preserving $s,t$-reachability to achieve a smaller space bound. All three can be modified to yield an algorithm for unweighted distance. Our contribution is to define an approximation to the walk polynomial in weighted graphs that allows us to infer weighted $s,t$-distance in sublinear $\mathsf{CLP}$. We do so by non-trivially combining elements from each of the above three papers.

items.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
items.summary: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

items.title: A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Hypergraph Unreliability
items.summary: We give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for all-terminal unreliability in explicitly represented undirected hypergraphs of arbitrary rank. The algorithm estimates the probability that independent hyperedge failures disconnect the hypergraph, allowing a different rational failure probability for every edge. For a common failure probability, this improves the quasi-polynomial approximation schemes of Cen, Li, and Panigrahi to polynomial time and answers the polynomial-time approximation question reiterated in their subsequent work on graphs. The construction turns their representative-survival bound into an importance sampler whose relative second moment is bounded solely in terms of the number of vertices. We protect one randomly chosen representative pair during contraction, correct the path likelihood, and divide by the number of pairs surviving at the end. The resulting unbiased estimator has relative second moment at most $\binom n2$, even when unreliability is exponentially small. A minimum-cut normalization makes this estimator implementable with polynomially bounded precision: the residual likelihood becomes a survival probability in an auxiliary absorbing process, which admits rational discretization with a fixed random-bit budget. Logarithmic rate rounding and an exact weighted minimum cut extend the construction to unequal rational failure probabilities. The algorithm's worst-case running time and random-bit usage are polynomial in the input length, the inverse relative error, and $\log(1/δ)$ for confidence $1-δ$.

items.title: Extending Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization to Systems of Linear Equations
items.summary: Solving systems of linear equations, $Ax=b$, is a ubiquitous task in computational science. The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd algorithm requires phase estimation, controlled rotations, and post-selection, impractical on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware. We extend sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), developed for quantum chemistry, to linear systems. Following the sample-based Krylov variant, the Hermitian matrix $A$ is decomposed in the Pauli basis, the Trotterized time evolution of $|b\rangle$ is sampled at several times to select computational-basis configurations, and the system is solved classically by a Galerkin projection onto the selected subspace. We prove that the subspace solution is exact when the sampled configurations contain the Krylov support of $b$ and optimal in the energy norm for symmetric positive-definite matrices, so that noise-induced configurations cannot degrade it as long as they do not displace the ideal ones. On IBM Quantum hardware, the sampled distribution of a $4\times4$ example deviates from the exact one by eleven times the shot-noise level, yet the solution is recovered exactly. For a localized problem of dimension $N=1024$, SQD selects 33 configurations, reaches a relative error of $10^{-5}$, and its truncated subspaces coincide with the optimal choice; readout errors enlarge the subspace without degrading the accuracy. The tests also show the limitations: the selected subspace coincides with that of inexpensive classical selection, banded matrices require exponentially many Pauli terms in the binary encoding, and Trotter errors populate spurious configurations unless the circuits are deep. An MIT-licensed Python package and notebooks that reproduce the numerical results are provided.

items.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
items.summary: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

items.title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number
items.summary: We consider here computational homogenization of a periodic two-phase conduction problem. Quantum linear-system algorithms for its finite element discretization are limited by the condition number of the stiffness matrix. This condition number grows quadratically with the number of elements per side. Classically, preconditioning by the homogeneous (single-phase) operator bounds the condition number by the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size. On a quantum computer, however, a preconditioner encoded as a separate factor multiplies the subnormalizations, and the quadratic dependency returns. In this paper, we absorb the closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator into the finite element factors. The preconditioned operator then becomes the product of a norm-preserving gradient operator $\mat{V}$, a diagonal matrix of scaled conductivities, and $\mat{V}^T$. Each factor has norm at most one. The block encoding therefore has subnormalization one, and its condition number is bounded by just the conductivity contrast, for every mesh size and in every dimension. The operator $\mat{V}$ is applied as a quantum Fourier transform, a small rotation at each wavenumber, and an inverse transform. Quantum singular value transformation then block-encodes the inverse of the preconditioned operator. We test the method numerically on three periodic cells with up to $10^6$ unknowns. The results confirm that the condition number does not depend on the mesh, and the energy-norm error of the inverse is below the polynomial tolerance at every mesh. On meshes of $4 \times 4$ and $8 \times 8$ elements, we also build the entire inverse as one Qiskit circuit and simulate it by state vector, with the rotation at each wavenumber built from uniformly controlled rotations. The output state agrees with the finite element solution to within the polynomial tolerance.

items.title: A Better Lower Bound for Sublinear Metric Steiner Tree
items.summary: In the metric Steiner tree problem, we are given an $n$-point metric space $(V,w)$ and a set of terminals $T\subseteq V$, and we are interested in the smallest total weight $\mathsf{st}(V,T,w)$ of a tree that contains every terminal and may also use points of $V\setminus T$. We work in the distance-oracle model: the algorithm knows $V$ and $T$ in advance and learns $w$ only by querying a single entry $w(u,v)$ at a time. The goal is to estimate $\mathsf{st}(V,T,w)$ with the minimum number of queries. A factor of $2$ is achievable with nearly linear number of queries, so the interesting question is the query complexity of algorithms with an approximation ratio strictly below $2$. We prove that for every fixed $η\in(0,1)$, every randomized $(2-η)$-approximation algorithm must make more than $\widetildeΩ(n^{7/5})$ queries, improving upon the previously known bound of $\widetildeΩ(n^{6/5})$. Given that the best known upper bound shows that $\widetilde O(n^{5/3})$ queries suffice, the exponent of this problem now lies between $7/5$ and $5/3$, up to logarithmic factors.

items.title: Boundary stabilization of a moving interface in a 2 x 2 weakly hyperbolic system of balance laws: application to continuous sedimentation
items.summary: We design a boundary feedback for the level of the sediment bed of a continuous settler and prove that it exponentially stabilizes the linearized closed loop under a small-gain condition. The unit is modeled by a 2 x 2 system of balance laws in which the bed surface, the interface, is not a smooth part of the solution but a moving shock between a weakly hyperbolic free-settling zone and a strictly hyperbolic compression zone. We describe it by the Rankine-Hugoniot relations and map the problem onto a fixed domain. Moreover, we prove local well-posedness with a continuation criterion given by a single margin function. Then we linearize the system near an equilibrium. The linearization couples a dissipative distributed layer to one scalar, the interface position, whose equation does not contain the control. We solve this by infinitedimensional forwarding: a Sylvester kernel cancels the interface trace and isolates the interface pole, and a proportional feedback then sets its decay rate. Every hypothesis is verified on an illustrative example, a laboratory-scale continuous settler containing a bed of compact polystyrene beads.

items.title: A Gaussian Process Regression-Enhanced Two-Sweep Parameterized Power Method for Computing Extreme Eigenpairs
items.summary: For computing the dominant eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvector of a real and symmetric matrix, inspired by the parameterized power method and multistep iteration, we propose a two-sweep parameterized power method, and establish its convergence theory. To further improve the convergence speed of the new method, we use Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict the quasi-optimal parameter and give a version of the proposed method based on GPR. Numerical experiments show that the two-sweep parameterized power method with quasi-optimal parameters outperforms some existing methods in terms of computing efficiency.

items.title: Lowered crossover points of Anthropic's subexponential 3-SAT algorithm
items.summary: The October 2026 refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis count satisfying assignments in time $2^{o(n)}$, but an asymptotic bound does not say from which input size, the crossover point, they beat the best known algorithms. We make the #3-SAT recursion of Anthropic's algorithm explicit and lower its crossover points, computed from the main term of the proved bound, by proved changes. For the bound in the number $m$ of clauses, at clause density one, the crossover point drops to about $2^{420}$ clauses from $2^{33858}$; for general 3-SAT, in the number $n$ of variables, our estimate drops to $2^{8.6\cdot10^9}$ variables from $2^{2.2\cdot10^{12}}$. With integer tables the recursion counts, for every $j$, the assignments satisfying exactly $j$ clauses in time $2^{O(m/\sqrt{\log m})}$. We observe that this refutes the Sparse Max-3-SAT Hypothesis of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, which also follows from either refutation by the reduction of Impagliazzo, Paturi and Zane, and we lower the crossover point of this computation to about $2^{1016}$ clauses from $2^{68364}$. The distance is structural: we define a rewrite-and-merge class that contains the recursion and all our constructions, and prove that in the main-term model no grid algorithm in it can gain for general 3-SAT below about $2^{6000}$ variables. For two balanced homogeneous merges we prove with quantum functionals an exponent of at least $(\log_2K)^{-3}$ per edge bit, which excludes running times $2^{n^{1-c}}$. Independently of SAT, we formalise the algorithm as a model of computation, Signed Network Sums, which contains rank-one methods and contraction trees. On the complete graph with four nodes, one-level constructions contract the network in $N^{23/6}$ if $ω=2$ and in about $N^{3.93}$ on the current (preprint) matrix-multiplication curve, below the bound $N^4$ of every rank-one method or contraction tree.

items.title: List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time
items.summary: A class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ is tame if there is a constant c such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has at most $n^c$ minimal separators. Many important graph classes are tame, including chordal graphs, permutation graphs, and circle graphs. Several fundamental problems, most notably Max Weight Independent Set, can be solved in polynomial time on every tame class, which explains in a unified way their tractability on all these classes. We show that List 3-Coloring can be solved in quasipolynomial time on every tame class of graphs.

items.title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
items.summary: We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+κ)\log(1/ε))$ for expected squared solution error $ε$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $κ$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.

items.title: An energy-constrained implicit step-and-truncate algorithm and its robust error estimates
items.summary: Deriving mesh-robust error bounds is an open problem for low-rank methods, including dynamical low-rank (DLR) and step-and-truncate (SAT) approaches, as highlighted in a recent review. Existing bounds can depend on Lipschitz constants that grow with inverse mesh size, making them impractical, particularly for kinetic equations, a major application of low-rank methods. We develop a unified framework for implicit SAT that provides a discrete counterpart of energy-localization analysis for nonlinear partial differential equations. By restricting numerical solutions to energy-localized regions, we obtain one-sided Lipschitz stability with constants independent of spatial resolution. The resulting error estimates and time-step restrictions are mesh robust, answering this open problem for the class of implicit SAT schemes covered by our assumptions. We emphasize that energy localization provides a general mechanism for mesh-independent robust error estimates in low-rank approximation, extending beyond the SAT methods considered here. Analogous results for DLR methods will be presented in subsequent work. Returning to implicit SAT, we demonstrate the broad applicability of the framework through error estimates for different classes of equations. Specifically, for semilinear parabolic and Vlasov--Poisson equations, we establish robust first-order error bounds for backward-Euler SAT under suitable regularity assumptions. Energy localization also has practical implications. We design an energy-constrained implicit SAT algorithm. Implicit SAT methods without energy constraints can select incorrect solution branches even when their algebraic residuals are small. Moreover, time-step reduction can be essential for continuation into larger energy regions. Numerical experiments support these conclusions.

items.title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
items.summary: Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.

items.title: Exact construction of quasi-uniform designs over polytopal domains
items.summary: We develop two sampling algorithms for constructing extensible designs with mesh ratio at most two on finite unions of full-dimensional rational convex polytopes. Starting from a rational initial point, both algorithms produce rational coordinates and perform the geometric comparisons governing point selection exactly. This ensures that distance ties and geometric degeneracies are handled without rounding ambiguity, preserving the prescribed selection rules and mesh-ratio guarantee at every stage. The first algorithm, Local Exact Farthest-Point Sampling (LEFPS), implements a prescribed farthest-point rule by local updates of the restricted Voronoi diagram. The second algorithm, Arithmetic-Aware Admissible Sampling (AAS), minimizes the representation length of reduced rational coordinates over admissible fragment vertices and edge midpoints. Since the cost of exact arithmetic depends on coordinate lengths, we analyze both operation counts and bit complexity. For fixed dimension and input, each sampling rule admits an $O(N\log N)$ unit-cost implementation and a separate implementation with $\widetilde O(L_N)$ bit complexity, where $L_N$ is the total length of the output coordinates. On rational interval covers, every admissible sequence from the vertex-midpoint candidate set has logarithmic coordinate height. We also identify the ordered sequences explicitly for LEFPS on interval unions and four-dimensional coordinate-order domains, and for AAS on a rectangle and a nonconvex cross. These descriptions yield direct generation with $O(N)$ unit-cost work and optimal $Θ(N\log N)$ bit work, including exact quality measures at every prefix. Numerical experiments compare local Voronoi maintenance, coordinate growth, and direct generation.

items.title: Polynomially Solvable Cases of the Quadratic Binary Optimization Problem with a Fixed Cardinality Constraint
items.summary: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems and their variant with a fixed cardinality constraint are both well-known NP-hard problems. While certain structural properties of the cost matrix can make some QUBO instances solvable in polynomial time, this advantage typically disappears once a cardinality constraint is added. In this work, we investigate specific structural conditions on the cost matrix under which the constrained version-quadratic binary optimization with a fixed cardinality-remains tractable.

items.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
items.summary: Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots that start and end at rest, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories, provide a numerical algorithm for computing them, and discuss how these insights may improve the performance of existing numerical trajectory optimizers.

items.title: An Efficient Randomized Hierarchical Tucker Decomposition
items.summary: We introduce randomized algorithms for computing the hierarchical Tucker decomposition of high-order tensors. Unlike traditional algorithms performed in a sequential leaves-to-root direction, our algorithms traverse the dimension tree in a root-to-leaves direction, leveraging randomized sequential projections to accelerate the computation of intermediate subspaces. This strategy can reduce the computation time by an order of magnitude relative to prior randomized algorithms using the leaves-to-root direction, while guaranteeing quasi-optimal approximation. Although the theoretical error bound is slightly larger than for leaves-to-root methods, in all our experiments the practical error adheres to the classic bound. Our results highlight the method's potential for scalable tensor decompositions in high-dimensional data analysis.

items.title: Numerical methods for nonlinear stochastic differential equations driven by subdiffusion
items.summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by subdiffusion see great applications in anomalous transport and asset price dynamics. Trusted numerical methods are essential for their application in practice. In this paper, for SDEs driven by subdiffusion with superlinear coefficients, we propose a brand-new explicit numerical method. The sharp convergence rate is proved with new techniques. The potential application of the proposed method in numerically solving a generalized Fokker-Planck equation is also illustrated. Numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the theoretical results.

items.title: A Parallel Heuristic for the Fixed Cardinality Binary Quadratic Program
items.summary: The Fixed Cardinality Binary Quadratic Program (FCBQP) is an optimization problem that requires a prescribed number of variables to take the value 1. We propose a parallel CPU-based heuristic that combines impact-based variable selection, tabu search, guided restarts, and a shared elite pool. Computational experiments on 342 benchmark instances from the maximum dispersion problem, k-clique problem, and minimum graph bisection problem show that the new algorithm is competitive and can reach best-known or reference values on instances with more than 20000 variables within one minute.

items.title: Distributed Grid Search for Hyperparameter Tuning
items.summary: The performance of many distributed optimization algorithms over peer-to-peer networks strongly depends on the choice of their hyperparameters. However, existing selection rules often require global quantities, yield conservative choices, or are tied to specific algorithms and hyperparameters. We propose Distributed Grid Search (D-GS), a consensus-based search method that evaluates and selects hyperparameter configurations across the network, requiring only the ability to run the tuned algorithm and evaluate local gradients. We also propose a zoom-in variant, Distributed Zoom Grid Search (D-ZGS), which improves empirical performance at a reduced cost. We prove that both methods terminate in finite time with all agents holding the same hyperparameter configuration, and quantify the (sub)optimality of this configuration. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression show that D-GS closely matches a centralized reference and that tuning and deployment cost a fraction of deploying algorithms with hyperparameters tuned using theoretical results.

items.title: Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
items.summary: This paper focuses on the use of learning nonlinear operators via Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) for approximating the solutions of optimal control problems. We study two operator learning strategies, namely, indirect and direct, both based on DeepONets, for parametric families of optimal control problems where the same problem must be solved many times for different initial data, different parameters, different cost function weights, and different bounds defining the set of the admissible controls. In the indirect strategy two DeepONets approximate the solution operators of the state and adjoint systems, and their predictions are used inside iterative projected gradient algorithms for finding the optimal control. In the direct strategy, a single DeepONet approximates the operator that maps directly to the optimal control generated by a reference solver; consequently, a new control is obtained through a single evaluation of the network. In order to analyze the computational cost, the efficiency, the speed and the accuracy of the learning strategies, we consider an optimal control problem related to an ordinary differential system that describes the temporal evolution of the glioblastoma growth subject to therapeutic interventions. For this specific optimal control problem we propose a discretize-then-optimize strategy, based on an implicit-explicit finite difference method, and then, we develop several numerical experiments in order to compare the two DeepONet learning strategies for this problem. The proposed operator learning DeepONet strategies can be adapted to approximate large classes of optimal control problems related to diverse differential systems.

items.title: Steiner Tree Parameterized by Multiway Cut: Single-Exponential Time and Polynomial Space
items.summary: In the Steiner Tree problem, the goal is to find a minimum-weight tree containing a given set of terminals in an edge-weighted graph. Given a multiway cut of size $s$, we propose a deterministic algorithm running in $2^{O(s)}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)$ time and polynomial space ($n$ vertices, non-negative $b$-bit integer weights). A multiway cut for the terminals is a set of vertices whose deletion leaves at most one terminal in each connected component. This result answers a question of Jansen and Swennenhuis (ESA 2024). Building on their component decomposition, we show that it suffices to connect the selected cut vertices together with $O(s)$ additional terminals and attach the remaining terminals by shortest paths. We use colour coding to optimize over the choice of these additional terminals.

items.title: New bounds for online coloring three-colorable graphs
items.summary: We prove new lower and upper bounds for online coloring of three-colorable graphs, improving classical bounds of Vishwanathan [FOCS'1990] that have stood for more than three decades. For the lower bound against deterministic algorithms, we improve Vishwanathan's $Ω(\log^2n)$ to \(\exp\!\bigl(Ω((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})\bigr)\). For the upper bound of randomized algorithms, we give a randomized algorithm that achieves $O(\sqrt{n})$ improving Vishwanathan's $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$. Technically, for the lower bound construction, we introduce the language of $t$-fold coloring for simpler description of recursive construction, and the notion of post-degree for future control, and use the flexibility of two-sided colors of bipartite graph, constructed using the independent set amplification method of Vishwanathan, as building blocks to ensure three-colorability. The randomized algorithm integrates, in a new way, some of the ideas in offline coloring of Wigderson and Blum with ideas of Vishwanathan in the online setting, such as the degree control from Wigderson, the offline-monochromatic class from Blum, and the anchor-sampling from Vishwanathan and the CBIP algorithm by Lov{á}sz, Saks and Trotter.

items.title: Robust Principal Component Analysis via $\ell_0$ Alternating Minimization
items.summary: Robust principal component analysis concerns the recovery of a low-rank matrix $Z$ and a sparse matrix $S$ from their observed sum $D = Z + S$. In this paper, we study this recovery problem under an $\ell_0$ sparsity penalty and a rank constraint on the low-rank component. By exploiting the entrywise separable structure of the sparse subproblem, we obtain an exact closed-form solution via hard thresholding with box clipping, avoiding the shrinkage bias of $\ell_1$-based methods. The low-rank subproblem is solved by truncated SVD. We prove block-coordinate convergence of the resulting alternating minimization scheme, establish uniqueness of block minimizers under non-degeneracy and singular value gap conditions, establish local linear convergence under a contraction condition on the Fréchet derivative of the truncated SVD operator restricted to the sparse support, and provide a second-order optimality analysis via the Riemannian Hessian. Experiments on synthetic data, images, and video show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing convex and nonconvex algorithms, most notably in support recovery and in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

items.title: A well-balanced path-conservative discontinuous Galerkin method with generalized hydrostatic reconstruction for non-conservative balance laws
items.summary: We propose a high-order well-balanced path-conservative discontinuous Galerkin method for one-dimensional balance laws with non-conservative products. Generalized hydrostatic reconstruction at cell interfaces couples effective numerical fluxes with Dal Maso-LeFloch-Murat path integrals, while a cellwise reference-equilibrium decomposition cancels projection-induced residuals in the volume discretization. Under explicit assumptions on equilibrium recovery, admissibility, paths, and boundary data, the spatial discretization is path conservative, and prescribed rest and moving equilibria are exactly preserved by both the semi-discrete scheme and its fully discrete SSP-RK approximation. The framework is applied to the two-layer shallow water equations and a blood-flow model with spatially varying vessel properties. Numerical experiments confirm the designed order of accuracy and round-off-level preservation of smooth and discontinuous equilibria, demonstrate accurate resolution of small perturbations, and show that the interface treatment captures shocks and stationary material contacts without visible spurious oscillations.

items.title: A bounded degree SDSOS hierarchy for solving SPLD polynomial programs
items.summary: A polynomial optimization problem is said to have an SPLD structure if the polynomials defining its objective and constraints admit decompositions into separable and nonseparable parts, with the maximum degree of the separable parts exceeding that of the nonseparable parts. In this paper, we propose a bounded degree SDSOS hierarchy for globally solving a class of such problems. We establish the asymptotic convergence of this hierarchy over compact feasible sets and provide a sufficient condition for its finite convergence. Numerical experiments compare the proposed hierarchy with the BSDSOS hierarchy (Chuong et al. in J. Global Optim., 75(4):885-919, 2019).

items.title: Improved Approximation Guarantees for Periodic-Review Stochastic Inventory Control
items.summary: In periodic-review stochastic inventory control, replenishment policies must balance holding and backlogging costs while responding to uncertain demands and evolving forecasts that may be arbitrarily correlated and nonstationary. In this general information setting, Levi, P{á}l, Roundy, and Shmoys (Mathematics of Operations Research 2007) established that the fully adaptive optimum can be approximated within factor $2$, which had remained the best-known performance guarantee since then. Their marginal cost accounting and dual-balancing framework made this comparison possible without computing optimal decisions across future trajectories, opening a broad research program on approximation algorithms for stochastic inventory systems. We break this long-standing barrier for periodic-review stochastic inventory control, showing how to compete against the fully adaptive benchmark within factor $\frac{ e }{ e-1 } \approx 1.582$ while retaining general demand correlations and evolving forecasts. We attain these advances by discovering a structural connection between marginal inventory accounting and weighted stopping problems, where each unit's conditional holding charge forms a supermartingale, while postponing its order incurs a history-dependent backlog charge. To leverage the random thresholding approach of Ma and Tzamos (ICML 2023) in this context, we develop a potential-function analysis, leading to an $\frac{ e }{ e-1 }$-approximation with respect to any unit's stopping problem. Subsequently, our common-threshold policy coordinates these marginal decisions into a global replenishment policy without additional loss.

items.title: Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $ε$-close Surrogates
items.summary: Non-convex optimization is central to machine learning and AI, yet unlike its convex counterpart, it still lacks a general and principled framework. In this work, we try to highlight the importance of combining noisy perturbations with over-parametrization mathematically under the classic setting of matrix completion (MC). Matrix completion is an important non-convex recovery problem in which only a subset of a matrix's entries is observed, and the remaining entries must be recovered using low-rank constraints. This problem is notoriously difficult because observations are limited. However, we show that by injecting $ε$-level perturbations into the nullspace of the observation mask, we can construct noisy matrix sensing surrogates whose solutions remain $\mathcal{O}(ε)$-close to the ground truth with valid restricted isometry property (RIP) constants. The existence of RIP further enables powerful tensor frameworks to be applied with theoretical guarantees. This approach reflects a broader empirical trend in which stochasticity or noise improves the curvature of the optimization landscape, allowing over-parameterized (a.k.a large) models to better separate signal from noise. Assuming each matrix entry is observed independently, we establish quantitative recovery guarantees without explicit requirements on sampling rate or incoherence, and discuss how such assumptions can further strengthen our results.

items.title: LEO Constellation Analysis for Satellite IoT: An Analysis of Coverage Gaps and Retransmissions
items.summary: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations are a promising way to connect Internet of Things (IoT) devices beyond terrestrial coverage, yet the intermittent visibility of their satellites imposes hard constraints on system and protocol design. Coverage probability and other snapshot statistics, which are often computed without accounting for the terminal's latitude, are insufficient for this purpose. Designers also need the temporal structure of coverage: the rate of coverage gaps, their duration distribution and mean, and quantities such as the probability that a retransmission succeeds after an initial transmission has failed. We develop an ergodic framework for Walker Star constellations in which these quantities reduce to spatial integrals over a two-dimensional torus that can be evaluated efficiently. We validate the framework against a seven-day Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) simulation of the Iridium NEXT constellation and find close agreement for the coverage probability, the revisit-time distribution, and the retransmission success probability. A comparison of Walker Star configurations further shows that constellations with similar satellite counts can yield substantially different packet-delivery probabilities with at most one retransmission, depending on the number of orbital planes. The results show that the ergodic model accurately gives the long-run values that finite time-domain simulations can only approximate, providing researchers with a tractable basis for the analytical modelling of IoT connectivity over non-terrestrial networks (NTN).

items.title: Physically Constrained Kinematic Calibration for High-Precision Robotic Needle Guidance
items.summary: Percutaneous needle insertion is a common practice in minimally invasive procedures whose clinical success depends on accurate needle placement. However, achieving the necessary precision is a challenge for manual operators. Robotic assistance can improve targeting accuracy and reduce operator dependence, but residual millimeter-scale errors persist because nominal kinematic models do not fully represent the physical manipulator. This paper presents a robust bound-constrained kinematic calibration method designed to improve positional accuracy for a 6-Degree-of-Freedom (6-DoF) robotic needle-guidance manipulator. The approach uses physically plausible parameter ranges to regularize a compact 19-parameter geometric identification model. By treating these bounds as active optimization constraints rather than mere numerical safeguards, the framework effectively mitigates parameter coupling and overfitting, ensuring highly stable parameter identification. In simulation, the proposed method reduced end-effector Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 3.422 mm to 0.690 mm (a 79.8% improvement). In benchtop hardware experiments, the calibrated model achieved sub-millimeter validation accuracy, including 0.865 mm RMSE in experimental trajectory validation and 0.610 mm RMSE in a coordinate-lattice verification task. These results demonstrate that physically constrained kinematic calibration can enhance robotic needle-targeting accuracy, establishing a high-precision foundation for future clinical applications.

items.title: Beamfocusing Beyond the Near Field: Frequency Diverse Arrays for OFDM-ISAC Systems
items.summary: Traditional phased arrays (PAs) achieve near-field (NF) beamfocusing through spherical wavefront curvature, but lose this range selectivity in the far field (FF). Frequency diverse arrays (FDAs) instead introduce frequency offsets across antenna elements. These offsets synthesize a range-dependent beam whose beamdepth is governed by the aggregate frequency-offset span rather than the physical aperture, thereby extending finite beamdepth into the FF. Although FDAs have been extensively studied for radar, their broader potential for wireless communications remains largely unexplored. Accordingly, this article examines how this capability can support wireless communications and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). We compare PA and FDA focusing mechanisms, explain FDA coupling and periodicities, and assess coexistence with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). Integer-multiple offsets preserve alignment with the OFDM subcarrier grid and avoid offset-induced intercarrier interference under ideal synchronization, but require suitable symbol mapping and receiver processing. We also distinguish FDA beamdepth from waveform-based radar range resolution and discuss their complementary roles in sensing. For the configurations studied, FDAs offer no additional single-user spatial degrees of freedom. Interestingly, their principal benefit is multiuser separation through location division multiple access (LDMA). Numerical case studies under an idealized FDA channel model show that FDA-LDMA achieves higher sum-rates than PA-based schemes for users with small angular separation in the FF, even after accounting for the bandwidth reserved for frequency offsets.

items.title: Infeasible Momentum Orthogonalized Methods for Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold
items.summary: We study deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, explicitly allowing iterates to deviate from the manifold rather than enforcing feasibility via retraction at each step. We introduce Landom, a Landing-type method that constructs momentum in the relative-gradient direction, maps this update to its compact polar factor, and combines the resulting tangential step with a step along the negative gradient of the orthogonality penalty to improve feasibility. Under operator-to-nuclear smoothness, Landom achieves an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the averaged nuclear norm of the relative gradient with exact gradients, and an $O(T^{-1/4})$ bound in expectation with stochastic momentum, bounded variance, and a fixed batch size. Our analysis also provides explicit pathwise bounds on the orthogonality residual, including its dependence on the step size and initial infeasibility. To address the coupling between objective and feasibility correction in Landom, we further propose Landom+, a two-timescale variant in which the tangential and normal step sizes are decoupled. By keeping the normal step size fixed, Landom+ achieves tighter control over the orthogonality residual following an initial transient while maintaining the respective convergence rates for stationarity. Numerical experiments across a range of applications illustrate that the proposed algorithms remain competitive with established manifold optimization approaches.

items.title: A Dual-Guided Column-Generation-Based Matheuristic for Integrated Railroad Blocking
items.summary: Integrated railroad blocking is a central planning problem in freight railway operations, which requires coordinated decisions on block design, blocking sequences, and block routing. We propose a dual-guided column-generation-based matheuristic (DG-CGM) that uses linear programming (LP) dual information to identify promising transportation paths and incorporates them into restricted mixed-integer programs to improve feasible solutions. Starting from an initial plan built by construction, DG-CGM alternates destroy and local repair with path generation, which uses dual prices from restricted LPs of a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation to identify promising transportation paths. When local improvements continue to stagnate, we further apply joint repair to combine alternatives across demand groups. To address the coupling between logical and physical path pricing, we introduce a joint reduced cost that eliminates path-specific dual variables from pricing, enabling more efficient column identification through exact labeling algorithms. We evaluate the performance of DG-CGM on both generated instances and real-world cases.
